notes: Counts: HAS_262=39 + NO_262=2 + NOT_FOUND=3 + HTTP_ERROR=0 = 44. Per table: 2026-09-27 has 31 HAS + 1 NOT_FOUND = 32 unique; 2026-10-01 has 8 HAS + 2 NO_262 + 2 NOT_FOUND = 12 unique.

The 35-row table lists sodium (lines 194,195), bclib (200,204) and fzzy-config (212,213) twice; that is why 35 rows collapse to the 32 unique identities consumed here. The two tables are disjoint (no identity appears in both), so 32 + 12 = 44 with no overlap to reconcile.

Bucket rule as implemented: a project is matched only when its slug or its title normalizes to the same identity (lowercase, separators removed). Where the exact slug resolved, the direct project endpoint was used. Where two plausible candidates of the right project type existed, the bucket was kept NOT_FOUND and AMBIGUOUS was written into notes.

Three cases needed a judgement call and are flagged in their notes: extended-drawers-polymer-patch (matched by being the only artifact of that name, not by strict normalization), c2me (derived slug does not resolve; upstream slug is c2me-fabric), playercollars (derived slug returns 0 hits; matched by splitting the name).

Evidence class: every bucket above is direct evidence from the Modrinth API (JSON field values), not inference. The only interpretations are (a) that a search top hit 'is the same identity', recorded per row, and (b) the judgement calls in the note above.

Freshness: all responses were fetched in this run; project date_modified values observed range from 2026-05-30 to 2026-11-08, i.e. the 26.2 game-version tag exists at query time and support changes quickly. A re-run later may change NO_262 rows.

Deviation from the brief: (1) no custom User-Agent could be set - the fetch tool controls its own client identity; (2) the primary 26.2 test uses the project-level game_versions field returned by /v2/search and /v2/project rather than calling /project/{id}/version for all 44, because that endpoint returns full version bodies; it was instead cross-checked on 2 rows (particledrawing HAS, sound-visualizer NO) and agreed in both cases.

Not verified by this lane: that the Modrinth project is the exact jar that failed in the Forbric runs (no jar was downloaded and no file hash was compared), that loaders match the failing column per row, and anything about CurseForge.
No jar, no binary, no CDN download URL was requested; only /v2 JSON endpoints.
